sources.title: Bilala
sources.note: Identity, late-14th-century capture of Njimi, expulsion by Wadai about 1630, Lake Fitri and Yao, 5,000 km2, French occupation May 1909. The page for Yao Sultanate returns the same text (redirect); Yao, Chad has one sentence on the sultanate.

notes:
Bilala Kingdom (Kanem phase, then the Sultanate of Yao), additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row. Pages: Bilala (also reached as Yao Sultanate); Yao, Chad had one sentence only.

The Bilala page is about the people; it dates nothing before "about 1630" except "late 14th century" and "17th-20th centuries". 1380 is taken from the empire-of-kanem dossier (Kanem-Bornu page, "around the year 1380"), so the founding and 1380 gain are recorded at confidence 1. The Kanem and Bornu pages say the mai retook Kanem in the early 1500s and fought and treated with a Bilala mai in 1570-1603; the Bilala page says Wadai expelled the Bilala from Kanem about 1630. The Kanem keyframe follows the Bilala page and so overstates the Bilala domain between the early 1500s and 1630 (the empire-of-kanem dossier shows the mai holding Kanem after 1500, with a Bilala contest 1570-1603): reconcile if the viewer shows overlapping claims. The wadai-empire dossier starts in 1635 against "around 1630" here.
The Yao disc (40 km radius) is a stand-in from the page's "roughly 5,000 km2"; the sultanate's real extent is not given. Muhammad Gadai (late 19th century, exile of seven years in Wadai, installed by a Wadai invasion) and Hassan Absakin are on the page without dates and are not in the ledger; whether Yao was a Wadai vassal is not stated.
Gazetteer: Njimi, Yao, Lake Fitri (the lake gazetteer has no Fitri), Mulabis.
